statement: $("#command-show").show().html("intelmqctl run {0} {1} {2}".format(bot, display_cmd, msg ? "'" + msg.replace("'", "'\\''") + "'" : ""));//XX dry are not syntax-correct
cwe_name: Improper Encoding or Escaping of Output

exact_cwe_mechanism.evidence: The code prepares structured output for display using .html() method with user-controlled input, but only escapes single quotes for shell syntax, not HTML metacharacters like <, >, &, ", creating improper encoding for HTML context

connection.evidence: User input from #message-playground flows directly into .html() method via string interpolation: msg parameter → command string construction → jQuery .html() method → DOM injection

diff_causality.evidence: This is an added line that introduces the vulnerable output construction. Reverting would remove the entire display mechanism that improperly encodes HTML output

security_control.evidence: The required control is proper HTML encoding for user-controlled content displayed via .html(). The code attempts shell quote escaping but completely omits HTML encoding, creating a clear deficiency
security_control.required_control: HTML encoding/escaping for user-controlled content displayed via .html() method
security_control.control_requirement_evidence: CWE-116 requires proper encoding for the output context (HTML DOM). Using .html() with unescaped user input violates this requirement
existing_controls_checked: Single quote escaping for shell syntax (msg.replace("'", "'\\''")) which is irrelevant for HTML context
security_control.deficiency_evidence: No HTML encoding is applied before using .html() method. The shell quote escaping provides no protection against XSS via HTML metacharacters

concrete_impact.evidence: Cross-site scripting (XSS) allowing arbitrary JavaScript execution in the context of the IntelMQ Manager interface, potentially compromising user sessions and administrative functions

diff_counterfactual: If the candidate line were reverted, the command display functionality would be removed entirely, eliminating the XSS vulnerability introduced by improper HTML encoding of user-controlled content.
supporting_evidence: User input from #message-playground flows directly into .html() method
Only single quotes are escaped for shell syntax, but HTML metacharacters remain unencoded
The .html() method interprets content as HTML, not plain text
Comment indicates this is for learning/display purposes, confirming output intent
unresolved_facts: Whether the displayed command is ever executed or used beyond visualization
Browser security mechanisms that might mitigate the XSS impact
review_comment: User-controlled message content from #message-playground is inserted into the DOM via .html() method with only shell quote escaping, leaving HTML metacharacters unencoded. This creates an XSS vulnerability where attackers can inject arbitrary JavaScript. Replace .html() with .text() or properly HTML-encode the user input before display to prevent script execution in the command visualization panel.
